newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures close stronger on higher cash hogs.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures close stronger on higher cash hogs.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures generally closed stronger as support from cash markets offset spillover weakness from cattle pits, traders said.

"Fundamentally, tightness in supplies continued to drive this market," said Dennis Smith, broker with LIT division of First Options, referring to light hog marketings and overall light storage numbers for pork bellies.

Hogs closed 0.700 to 0.075 cent a lb higher paced by December at 58.675 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.725 cent a lb higher to 0.025 lower with only distant August down and active February up most at 76.700 cents.

Hog runs were not as large as some traders had expected Monday and packer demand was strong as pork prices generally held. Prices often weaken the week of Thanksgiving but this year have not eased as much as expected, sources said.
Cash hogs also are expected to trade steady to firmer Tuesday as hog markeings were seen light, traders said.

Locals, Rand Financials and Merrill Lynch bought December on the rally while Prudential Securities, RBH and Lind-Waldock bought February. Spreaders bought February and April and sold December early but short February hogs/long February bellies weighed down February hogs late, pit sources said.
In hog options, locals bought calls and sold puts on the rally, pit sources added.

Pork bellies rallied after a mixed start following Friday's USDA monthly Cold Storage Report. Some traders considered the report bearish but the majority looked at the 16.2 million lbs on hand as impetus for buying because it showed belly stocks at historically low levels, they said.
Commercials bought and further buying interest developed on news that Poland would import 90,000 tonnes of pork bellies in 1997. This lifted prices into fund short covering, they added.
"We'll go to 80 (cents) non-stop now," one trader said referring to the strong technical picture left by February's close above 76 cents on the fund demand.
Late buying by Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien and local short covering boosted belly futures prices into market-on-close and closing buy stops, pit sources said.
